course.title: SQL Masterclass
course.tagline: Zero to advanced, one module at a time.
course.standard: PostgreSQL-first, with MySQL, SQLite and SQL Server notes.
course.description: Module 13 teaches CASE, COALESCE, NULLIF, GREATEST and LEAST, three-valued logic, NULL joins, aggregates, constraints and conditional reporting.
outcomes: Use CASE in filtering and ordering
Bucket rows with CASE and GROUP BY
Handle NULL with COALESCE and NULLIF
Avoid NULL join and NOT IN traps

modules.title: CASE, Conditional Logic and NULL Handling
modules.goal: Express conditional logic correctly and treat NULL as unknown, not empty.

topics.title: Introduction to CASE
topics.simple: CASE SQL me if/else ki tarah conditional value deta hai.
topics.pro: CASE evaluates conditions in order and returns the value from the first matching branch, making it the standard SQL conditional expression.

example.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM students;

topics.title: Simple CASE
topics.simple: Simple CASE ek expression ko fixed values se compare karta hai.
topics.pro: The simple form CASE expression WHEN value THEN result compares one expression for equality against each WHEN value.
points: Use searched CASE for NULL or ranges.

example.sql: SELECT grade, CASE grade WHEN 'A' THEN 'Excellent' WHEN 'B' THEN 'Good' ELSE 'Needs work' END AS comment FROM enrollments;

topics.title: Searched CASE
topics.simple: Searched CASE har WHEN me arbitrary boolean condition leta hai.
topics.pro: The searched form CASE WHEN condition THEN result evaluates independent boolean conditions, so it can express ranges, NULL checks and compound logic.

example.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN marks >= 75 THEN 'B' WHEN marks IS NULL THEN 'Missing' ELSE 'C' END AS band FROM students;

topics.title: CASE Evaluation Order
topics.simple: CASE pehla true branch leta hai; baad wale branches chhoot jaate hain.
topics.pro: CASE stops at the first true condition, so a broad condition placed before a narrow one makes the narrow branch unreachable.
points: Order branches from specific to broad.

example.sql: SELECT marks, CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'Distinction' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM students;
example.output: Distinction is unreachable because 90 also passes.

topics.title: CASE in SELECT
topics.simple: SELECT list me CASE computed column banata hai.
topics.pro: CASE in the select list derives a label, bucket or flag without changing stored data.
points: It does not modify the table.
All branches should return compatible types.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM students;
example.output: Each row gets a derived result column.

topics.title: CASE in WHERE
topics.simple: WHERE me CASE conditional predicate bana sakta hai.
topics.pro: CASE can produce a boolean inside WHERE, but a plain OR/AND expression is usually clearer and more index-friendly.
points: CASE must return a boolean here.

example.sql: SELECT name FROM students WHERE CASE WHEN marks IS NULL THEN FALSE ELSE marks >= 60 END;
example.output: Students with a known passing mark.

topics.title: CASE in ORDER BY
topics.simple: CASE se custom sort order define kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: CASE in ORDER BY maps values to sort ranks, enabling a business-defined order instead of alphabetical or numeric order.
points: The CASE is evaluated per row.

example.sql: SELECT title FROM courses ORDER BY CASE title WHEN 'SQL' THEN 1 WHEN 'Python' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;
example.output: SQL first, Python second, everything else after.

topics.title: CASE in GROUP BY
topics.simple: CASE se rows ko custom buckets me group kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: Grouping by a CASE expression creates buckets such as pass/fail or grade bands, and each bucket can then be aggregated.

example.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students GROUP BY result;

topics.title: CASE with Aggregates
topics.simple: CASE aggregate ke andar conditional value deta hai.
topics.pro: CASE inside SUM or COUNT lets one query compute several conditional totals without scanning the table repeatedly.
points: SUM(CASE ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts conditions.
COUNT(CASE ... THEN 1 END) counts non-null matches.

example.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students;

topics.title: Conditional Aggregation
topics.simple: Conditional aggregation ek hi pass me multiple metrics deta hai.
topics.pro: Conditional aggregation combines CASE or FILTER with aggregates to produce pass counts, fail counts and totals in one grouped query.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE marks >= 60) AS passed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE marks < 60) AS failed FROM students;

topics.title: COALESCE
topics.simple: COALESCE pehla non-null value deta hai.
topics.pro: COALESCE returns the first non-null argument, making it the standard way to supply a fallback for nullable columns.
points: Arguments are evaluated left to right.

example.sql: SELECT name, COALESCE(email, 'none') AS email FROM students;

topics.title: NULLIF
topics.simple: NULLIF equal values ko NULL bana deta hai.
topics.pro: NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL when a equals b and otherwise returns a; it is commonly used to turn zero denominators or blank strings into NULL.
points: The result type follows the first argument.

example.sql: SELECT marks / NULLIF(marks, 0) AS ratio FROM students;
example.output: NULL instead of division by zero.

topics.title: GREATEST and LEAST
topics.simple: GREATEST maximum aur LEAST minimum choose karte hain.
topics.pro: GREATEST returns the largest argument and LEAST the smallest; in PostgreSQL they ignore NULL arguments and return NULL only when every argument is NULL.

example.sql: SELECT GREATEST(marks, 0) AS floored, LEAST(marks, 100) AS capped FROM students;

topics.title: NULL and Three-Valued Logic
topics.simple: NULL unknown hai, false nahi.
topics.pro: SQL logic has three values: TRUE, FALSE and UNKNOWN; comparisons with NULL produce UNKNOWN, and WHERE keeps only TRUE rows.
points: NULL is not zero or empty.
UNKNOWN is filtered out by WHERE.

example.sql: SELECT NULL = NULL AS equal, NULL IS NULL AS is_null;

topics.title: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL
topics.simple: NULL check ke liye IS NULL use karo, = NULL nahi.
topics.pro: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL are the only direct NULL tests; equality with NULL is always UNKNOWN.
points: IS NOT NULL matches known values.

example.sql: SELECT name FROM students WHERE email IS NULL;

topics.title: NULL in Joins and IN
topics.simple: NULL join keys match nahi karte; NOT IN NULL se empty ho sakta hai.
topics.pro: Equality joins skip NULL keys, and a NULL in a NOT IN list makes the predicate UNKNOWN for every row.
points: Use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM for null-safe matching.

example.sql: SELECT name FROM students WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM enrollments WHERE student_id IS NOT NULL);
example.output: Students whose id is not in the known list.

topics.title: NULL in Aggregates and GROUP BY
topics.simple: Aggregates NULL ignore karte hain; GROUP BY NULL ko ek group banata hai.
topics.pro: COUNT(column), SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip NULL, while GROUP BY treats all NULLs as one group; COUNT(*) still counts every row.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows, COUNT(marks) AS known FROM students;

topics.title: NULL in Constraints and Uniqueness
topics.simple: CHECK NULL par pass hota hai; UNIQUE multiple NULLs allow karta hai.
topics.pro: A CHECK constraint passes when its expression is UNKNOWN, so a nullable column needs NOT NULL to enforce presence; a regular UNIQUE constraint allows multiple NULLs.
points: UNIQUE allows multiple NULLs unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT.

example.sql: SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks IS NULL;

topics.title: Common CASE and NULL Errors
topics.simple: Missing END, WHEN NULL aur = NULL sabse common mistakes hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are a missing END, a simple CASE trying to match NULL, an unreachable branch, equality with NULL and NOT IN with a NULL subquery.

example.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN marks IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE marks END AS safe_marks FROM students;

topics.title: Practical Conditional Reporting
topics.simple: CASE aur NULL handling ko reports me combine karo.
topics.pro: A reliable conditional report handles missing values explicitly, orders buckets intentionally and verifies that every row falls into exactly one branch.
points: Check the totals against the row count.

example.sql: SELECT COALESCE(CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN marks >= 75 THEN 'B' WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'C' WHEN marks IS NOT NULL THEN 'F' END, 'Missing') AS band, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students GROUP BY band ORDER BY band;
example.output: Grade-band counts with a missing bucket.

learn.q: What does CASE return?
options: A value from the first matching branch
learn.answer: A value from the first matching branch
learn.why: CASE is a conditional expression.

learn.q: Which CASE form supports ranges?
learn.why: Searched CASE accepts arbitrary boolean conditions.

learn.q: Which CASE form compares one expression for equality?
learn.why: Simple CASE is equality-only.

learn.q: Does simple CASE WHEN NULL match a NULL value?
learn.why: Equality with NULL is UNKNOWN; use searched CASE with IS NULL.

learn.q: What happens if no branch matches and there is no ELSE?
learn.why: ELSE is optional and defaults to NULL.

learn.q: Which branch wins when several conditions are true?
learn.why: CASE stops at the first true condition.

learn.q: Where can CASE be used?
options: In SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and GROUP BY
learn.answer: In SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and GROUP BY
learn.why: CASE is an expression usable wherever a value is accepted.

learn.q: What does COALESCE return?
learn.why: It supplies a fallback for NULL.

learn.q: What does NULLIF(a, b) return when a = b?
learn.why: NULLIF turns equal values into NULL.

learn.q: What is NULLIF commonly used to prevent?
learn.why: NULLIF(denominator, 0) turns a zero denominator into NULL.

learn.q: Does PostgreSQL GREATEST ignore NULL arguments?
learn.why: It ignores NULL and returns NULL only if all arguments are NULL.

learn.q: What does NULL = NULL evaluate to?
learn.why: NULL is not equal to anything, including itself.

learn.q: Which predicate matches NULL?
learn.why: Only IS NULL directly tests for NULL.

learn.q: What does WHERE do with UNKNOWN?
learn.why: WHERE keeps only TRUE rows.

learn.q: Do NULL join keys match each other?
learn.why: Equality with NULL is UNKNOWN.

learn.q: What does a NULL in a NOT IN list do?

learn.why: COUNT(*) counts rows, not values.

learn.why: COUNT(column) skips NULL.

learn.why: NULLs compare equal for grouping.

interview.q: What is CASE?
interview.answer: A standard SQL conditional expression that returns the value of the first matching branch.

interview.q: What is the difference between simple and searched CASE?
interview.answer: Simple CASE compares one expression for equality; searched CASE evaluates independent boolean conditions.

interview.q: Why does simple CASE fail to match NULL?
interview.answer: It uses equality, and NULL = NULL is UNKNOWN; use searched CASE with IS NULL.

interview.q: What happens when no CASE branch matches?
interview.answer: Without ELSE the result is NULL.

interview.q: What does COALESCE do?
interview.answer: Returns the first non-null argument, or NULL if all are null.

interview.q: What does NULLIF do?
interview.answer: Returns NULL when the two arguments are equal, otherwise the first argument.

interview.q: Why use NULLIF(denominator, 0)?
interview.answer: It turns a zero denominator into NULL, avoiding division by zero.

interview.q: How do GREATEST and LEAST treat NULL in PostgreSQL?
interview.answer: They ignore NULL arguments and return NULL only when every argument is NULL.

interview.q: What are the three SQL truth values?
interview.answer: TRUE, FALSE and UNKNOWN.

interview.q: What is NULL?
interview.answer: A marker for an unknown or missing value, not zero or an empty string.

interview.q: Why does = NULL never match?
interview.answer: Equality with NULL is UNKNOWN, and WHERE keeps only TRUE.

interview.q: When should you use IS NULL?
interview.answer: Whenever you need to test whether a value is missing.

interview.q: Why is NOT IN risky with NULLs?
interview.answer: A NULL in the list makes the predicate UNKNOWN for every row, potentially returning no rows.

interview.q: How do you do a null-safe equality join?
interview.answer: Use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM when NULL should match NULL.

interview.q: How do aggregates treat NULL?
interview.answer: COUNT(column), SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX ignore NULL; COUNT(*) counts rows.

interview.q: How does GROUP BY treat NULL?
interview.answer: It groups all NULLs together as one group.

interview.q: How does a CHECK constraint treat NULL?
interview.answer: The check passes because NULL yields UNKNOWN, not FALSE; NOT NULL is needed to require a value.

interview.q: How does UNIQUE treat NULL?
interview.answer: A regular UNIQUE constraint allows multiple NULLs; PostgreSQL 15+ can use NULLS NOT DISTINCT.

interview.q: How do you count passed and failed rows in one query?
interview.answer: Use conditional aggregation with CASE or FILTER.

interview.q: Why order CASE branches carefully?
interview.answer: The first true branch wins, so a broad branch can make later specific branches unreachable.

labs.title: Simple CASE
labs.task: Label letter grades as Excellent, Good or Needs work.
labs.solution: SELECT grade, CASE grade WHEN 'A' THEN 'Excellent' WHEN 'B' THEN 'Good' ELSE 'Needs work' END AS comment FROM enrollments;

labs.title: Searched CASE
labs.task: Band marks into A, B, C or Missing.
labs.solution: SELECT name, CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN marks >= 75 THEN 'B' WHEN marks IS NULL THEN 'Missing' ELSE 'C' END AS band FROM students;

labs.title: Case order
labs.task: Write a CASE where distinction is reachable.
labs.solution: SELECT marks, CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'Distinction' WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result FROM students;

labs.title: CASE in WHERE
labs.task: Return students with a known passing mark.
labs.solution: SELECT name FROM students WHERE CASE WHEN marks IS NULL THEN FALSE ELSE marks >= 60 END;

labs.title: CASE in ORDER BY
labs.task: Order SQL first, Python second, others last.
labs.solution: SELECT title FROM courses ORDER BY CASE title WHEN 'SQL' THEN 1 WHEN 'Python' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;

labs.title: CASE in GROUP BY
labs.task: Count pass and fail buckets.
labs.solution: SELECT CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END AS result, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students GROUP BY result;

labs.title: Conditional SUM
labs.task: Return passed and total counts.
labs.solution: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students;

labs.title: FILTER alternative
labs.task: Return passed and failed counts with FILTER.
labs.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE marks >= 60) AS passed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE marks < 60) AS failed FROM students;

labs.title: COALESCE
labs.task: Show none for a missing email.
labs.solution: SELECT name, COALESCE(email, 'none') AS email FROM students;
labs.expected: Every row has an email value.

labs.title: NULLIF
labs.task: Avoid division by zero with NULLIF.
labs.solution: SELECT marks / NULLIF(marks, 0) AS ratio FROM students;

labs.title: GREATEST and LEAST
labs.task: Clamp marks between 0 and 100.
labs.solution: SELECT GREATEST(marks, 0) AS floored, LEAST(marks, 100) AS capped FROM students;

labs.title: NULL comparison
labs.task: Show that NULL = NULL is UNKNOWN.
labs.solution: SELECT NULL = NULL AS equal, NULL IS NULL AS is_null;

labs.title: IS NULL
labs.task: Return students without an email.
labs.solution: SELECT name FROM students WHERE email IS NULL;

labs.title: Null-safe join
labs.task: Match students and applicants even when emails are NULL.
labs.solution: SELECT s.name, a.marks FROM students s JOIN applicants a ON s.email IS NOT DISTINCT FROM a.email;

labs.title: NOT IN with NULL
labs.task: Return students not in a known id list, safely.
labs.solution: SELECT name FROM students WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM enrollments WHERE student_id IS NOT NULL);

labs.title: Count NULLs
labs.task: Count all rows and known marks.
labs.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_count, COUNT(marks) AS known FROM students;

labs.title: Check NULL constraint
labs.task: Show that a CHECK allows a NULL mark.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Zara', NULL) RETURNING id, marks;

labs.title: Unique NULLs
labs.task: Insert two students with NULL emails.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, email) VALUES ('A', NULL), ('B', NULL) RETURNING id, email;

labs.title: Conditional report
labs.task: Count grade bands including Missing.
labs.solution: SELECT COALESCE(CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN marks >= 75 THEN 'B' WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'C' WHEN marks IS NOT NULL THEN 'F' END, 'Missing') AS band, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students GROUP BY band ORDER BY band;

labs.title: CASE in UPDATE
labs.task: Replace NULL marks with zero.
labs.solution: UPDATE students SET marks = CASE WHEN marks IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE marks END RETURNING id, marks;

logic.q: Why does branch order matter in CASE?
logic.answer: The first true branch wins, so a broad condition can shadow a later specific condition.

logic.q: Why does simple CASE not match NULL?
logic.answer: It uses equality, and NULL = NULL is UNKNOWN, not TRUE.

logic.q: Why is CASE in WHERE often a bad idea?
logic.answer: It can hide index-friendly predicates and make the filter harder for the planner to optimize.

logic.q: Why use COALESCE instead of CASE for a fallback?
logic.answer: COALESCE expresses the first-non-null intent directly and is shorter.
It converts a zero denominator into NULL, so the division returns NULL instead of erroring.

logic.q: Why do GREATEST and LEAST behave differently across databases?
logic.answer: PostgreSQL ignores NULL arguments, while some databases return NULL if any argument is NULL.

logic.q: Why is NULL not equal to zero?
logic.answer: NULL means unknown or missing; zero is a known numeric value.
WHERE keeps only rows whose predicate is TRUE; UNKNOWN is not TRUE.

logic.q: Why is NOT IN unsafe with NULLs?
logic.answer: A NULL in the list makes the comparison UNKNOWN for every row, so nothing is returned.

logic.q: Why use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM in a join?
logic.answer: It treats NULL as equal to NULL when the business rule requires matching missing keys.

logic.q: Why does COUNT(*) include NULL rows?
logic.answer: It counts rows, not values, so NULL columns do not matter.
It counts only known values in that column.

logic.q: Why do NULLs form one GROUP BY group?
logic.answer: Grouping treats NULLs as equal to each other for partitioning.

logic.q: Why does a CHECK constraint allow NULL?
logic.answer: A CHECK rejects only FALSE; NULL produces UNKNOWN, which passes.

logic.q: Why does UNIQUE allow multiple NULLs?
logic.answer: NULLs are not considered equal for a regular unique index; use NULLS NOT DISTINCT if that is wrong.

debug.broken: SELECT name, CASE email WHEN NULL THEN 'missing' ELSE 'known' END AS state FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT name, CASE WHEN email IS NULL THEN 'missing' ELSE 'known' END AS state FROM students;

debug.fix: SELECT CASE WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END FROM students;

debug.fix: SELECT CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'Distinction' WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'Pass' ELSE 'Fail' END FROM students;

debug.title: Equals NULL

debug.fix: SELECT name FROM students WHERE email IS NULL;

debug.fix: CREATE TABLE t (marks INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (marks >= 0));
